sector_model: midstream natural gas pipelines and gathering (regulated and contracted infrastructure); use EBITDA, distributable cash flow, capex, leverage, dividend coverage; equity method investees
thesis: DT Midstream owns contracted natural gas pipelines and gathering. 9M26 revenue 1,015M (+9.6%), net income attributable 360M (+9.1%), operating cash flow 777M (+10.0%), management raised 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance to 1,185-1,225M and says 2.4B of organic projects are committed. At 113.66 it trades near 24.6x TTM GAAP earnings, 4.6% TTM FCF yield and 12.3x EV to guided adjusted EBITDA midpoint (management definition, includes proportional equity investees), with a 3.1% dividend yield (0.88 quarterly). Quality infrastructure; the price already reflects it.
counterthesis: Growth capex and a 352M annual dividend leave about 181M after dividends on TTM FCF 533M (66% payout of FCF), so growth is funded partly by debt. Net debt 3,069M is about 2.5x guided adjusted EBITDA, plus 140M noncontrolling interests. A key customer, Expand Energy, drives a significant share of revenue and Haynesville/Marcellus gas volumes depend on gas prices. 126M of capex sat in payables at 9/30 (83M a year ago), so cash capex understates spending incurred. Cash taxes are low (9M paid 9M26) while deferred tax is 116M of 777M OCF, a benefit that normalizes. Stonewall litigation with Antero (fees range 0-4.9M, appeal planned). Stock fell from 122.58 to 113.66 in three sessions, cause not identified.
invalidation: Loss of or volume cuts from Expand Energy; leverage above about 3.5x EBITDA; dividend coverage by FCF falling well below 1.0x after growth capex; cash taxes normalizing sharply higher without growth; slippage or cost overruns on the 2.4B committed projects.
